Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
Issued by National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
136 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably hot with highs in the 90s and heat index values
  100-107F each day.
  
- An isolated late day shower can't be ruled out along the
  seabreeze in the afternoons.
  
- Slightly better rain chances expected Thursday into early next
  week for the eastern and southern parts of the region as some 
  deeper moisture flows back inland. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 103 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

With exception to some light showers in the coastal counties,
conditions across the forecast area are dry (rain wise) and warm.
We could see some isolated to scattered showers and storms across
parts of the area this afternoon, and for the next few afternoons
during the work week; however, the ridge aloft centered over the
Desert SW will keep a lid on this activity. 

Going into the weekend and early next week, the aforementioned
ridge will shift more to the west, slightly losing its grip over 
the eastern and coastal counties. That along with a small bump up
in PWATs, and diurnal / seabreeze processes will allow for
somewhat higher PoPs in the afternoons. 

MaxTs for nearly the entire duration of this forecast period will
be at or around their climatological normals for this time of 
year. With that said and with dewpoints in the 70s, we are not 
looking at heat indices crossing into heat hazard territory.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 557 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Current satellite imagery depicts MVFR/IFR ceilings developing
over areas along and west of the Brazos River. These reduced
ceilings are anticipated to move into CLL and UTS over the next
couple of hours and may extend into CXO and IAH as well later this
morning. Additionally, periods of patchy fog have brought reduced
visibility to LBX as well. Based on yesterday, SGR may also experience
reduced visibility for a few hours around and shortly after 
sunrise. 

VFR conditions will return area-wide by 15Z. Light south-southwest 
winds early this morning will become southerly by the afternoon 
with wind speeds in the 8-12 kt range. Occasional gusts of 15-20
kt will be possible through the afternoon. Isolated SH/TS 
possible again this afternoon between 21Z-01Z mainly around the 
Houston metro terminals. Winds become light and variable 
overnight with potential for another round of patchy fog and 
reduced ceilings mainly west of I-45 going into Thursday morning.
Ceilings/visibilities improve back to VFR by 15Z on Thursday with
south to southeast winds around 8-12 kt prevailing. Another round
of isolated to scattered SH/TS possible in the afternoon.

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 103 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Winds and seas will be relatively low in the 10 to 15 kt range and
2 to 4 ft range respectively. A stray shower or two cannot be
ruled out during the afternoons, with convective activity more
likely towards the end of this work week and into next week.

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1229 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A typical summer weather pattern will prevail through this week
  with a few afternoon thunderstorms each day. 

- Afternoon highs will climb into the low to mid 90s each day 
  with maximum heat indices ranging from 101 to 109.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This afternoon through next Tuesday)
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Typical summer pattern looks to continue through our day-to-day 
forecast with little change expected. Upper level ridging is 
currently centered over New Mexico and a weak upper level trough 
situated in the eastern Gulf is leading to very weak upper level 
flow over our area. Diurnally driven showers will persist daily 
over sections of our area. Weak upper level flow will lead to slow
moving storms, but the average PWAT values dampen the chances for
flooding rainfall. 

A surface high pressure is situated over the eastern Gulf is
bringing light southerly winds over our area. Currently sporadic 
storms have began to initiate over much of the region. Outflow 
boundaries and cloud shading will likely keep heat indices from 
reaching the values required for a heat advisory. Modest DCAPE 
values suggest a small chance for localized strong downdrafts in 
convection through this afternoon.

Soileau

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

VFR conditions will prevail through the taf period. Scattered, 
diurnally driven, afternoon storms will continue with the highest 
risk at LFT and ARA. These storms will dissipate by 00Z this 
evening with skies clearing overnight. Another round of showers
and thunderstorms will develop after 16Z Thursday and continue
through the afternoon. Away from storms, light south southwesterly
winds will prevail. 

Jones

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Onshore winds are forecast to be 5-8 kts with gusts over 10 kts
possible. Isolated pulse storms are possible in the afternoons
with greater coverage closer to the coast.


&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

KBDI values continue to climb. Isolated showers and thunderstorms
are expected each afternoon will provide local relief but 
otherwise no widespread rain is expected. Minimum RH values will
be around 50%.

&&
